Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 3-day history of watery diarrhea, intermittent left lower abdominal cramp, initial vomiting and subjective fever, assessed as likely acute gastroenteritis; conservative management advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Loose, watery stools and increased frequency for 3 days (patient reports ~6–7 bowel movements/day).
  - Intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain, localized to the left side.
  - Initial vomiting at onset of illness; vomiting has now stopped.
  - Subjective fever/feeling hot at symptom onset; no measured temperature documented.
  - Weakness, shakiness, and reduced appetite; able to tolerate fluids (soups, smoothies, light/liquid foods).
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 3 days ago.
  - Vomiting occurred at the start and has resolved.
  - Diarrhea and crampy pain have persisted and are impacting daily activities and work.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors:
  - Ate a Chinese takeaway about 4 days ago (possible temporal association noted).
  - No specific relieving factors documented beyond resting and intake of fluids/light foods.
- Associated symptoms/systems review:
  - No visible blood in stool or vomit.
  - No ongoing fever documented at time of consult.
  - No diaphoresis/night sweats reported.
  - No current vomiting.
  - No other gastrointestinal diagnoses previously reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No reported blood in stools.
  - No current fever measured.
  - No ongoing vomiting.
  - No chronic bowel problems reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma — uses an inhaler; reported to be under control.
- No other chronic medical conditions documented.

Medications:
- Inhaler for asthma — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Recommended medications (by clinician during visit):
  - Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol recommended for fever/weakness: "two tablets up to four times a day" (strength not documented).
- Allergies:
  - None documented.

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Occupation: Accountant; has continued to attend work during illness.
- Smoking: Denies smoking.
- Alcohol: Denies alcohol use.
- No other substance use or social stressors documented.

Family History:
- No chronic family medical history documented.
- Household contact: one child vomited but did not have diarrhea; no other family members reported with identical symptoms.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs recorded in the transcript.
- No physical examination findings documented (examination was proposed but not performed/documented).

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or results available.
- Clinician noted stool sampling may be considered if symptoms persist.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrheal illness, likely gastroenteritis (presumed viral; bacterial etiology possible)
  - Assessment:
    - 3-day history of watery diarrhea, crampy left lower abdominal pain, initial vomiting, subjective fever, reduced appetite; likely infectious gastroenteritis.
  - Plan:
    - Conservative management: oral rehydration and maintenance of fluids.
    - Recommend oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) in the initial days — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Antipyretic/analgesic: paracetamol recommended (per clinician: two tablets up to four times daily; strength not documented).
    - No antibiotics recommended at this time.
    - Advise rest and time off work for 2–3 days while infection clears.
    - Advise returning for review if symptoms not improved in 3–4 days.
    - If symptoms persist or worsen, consider stool sampling and further investigations to evaluate for alternative causes or bacterial infection.
- Issue 2: Dehydration risk due to vomiting/diarrhea
  - Assessment:
    - Patient reports ongoing diarrhea with prior vomiting but currently tolerating fluids.
  - Plan:
    - Emphasize adequate oral fluids and use of rehydration solution.
    - Monitor for signs of dehydration; return earlier if unable to maintain oral intake, increasing weakness, dizziness, or reduced urine output.
- Issue 3: Impact on work/function
  - Assessment:
    - Frequent toilet use and weakness interfering with work; patient has been attending work despite symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Clinician advised 2–3 days off work to rest and allow recovery.

General Plan items:
- Safety-netting: return if no improvement in 3–4 days or if symptoms worsen; possible stool testing if ongoing.
- No investigations ordered during this consult.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (temperature, blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate).
  - No physical examination findings recorded.
  - No documented medication doses/strengths for inhaler or paracetamol.
  - No documented allergies (none recorded; allergy status should be confirmed).
  - No laboratory or stool test results; none obtained during consult.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Minor conflict regarding vomiting: initial response to "any vomiting?" was "no," then patient clarified he had vomited at the start of symptoms but has since stopped (conflict noted and reconciled in history).
  - Temperature: patient reported feeling hot at onset but did not provide a measured temperature.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio transcript is intelligible and contains sufficient clinical detail; occasional conversational fillers present but clinical information is clear.
